content:
In recent years, Macs have become increasingly affordable. The starting price has dropped, you get more memory and storage per dollar, and with the introduction of the MacBook Neo, Apple has for the first time become one of the most value-for-money options on the market.

Unfortunately, Apple has raised prices significantly due to ongoing memory shortages. Macs are no longer as attractive as they once were, but there are still some good deals out there—if you need a new computer, I would still say that a Mac is a good choice compared to other computer products on the market right now.

MacBook Air

Until the MacBook Neo launched, the MacBook Air was the entry-level choice in Apple's laptop lineup. Although the MacBook Neo makes its value proposition somewhat questionable, I would still say that if you want a better user experience without needing any high-end features, the MacBook Air is an excellent laptop.

MagSafe, P3 wide colour gamut display, Center Stage for the webcam, and longer battery life are just some of the highlights of the MacBook Air. It also comes in a 15-inch version, unlike the MacBook Neo which is only available in 13-inch.

MacBook Neo

This product doesn't need a long explanation—the MacBook Neo is Apple's first affordable MacBook, priced at just $699.

Compared to the MacBook Air mentioned above, there are some trade-offs, but at this price point it is still an incredible bargain. Build quality, display clarity, and the macOS experience are essentially uncompromised. Of course, you'll have to accept a slower A18 Pro chip (but honestly, it's not bad at all), fewer ports, and 8GB of memory, but at this price it's completely reasonable. It also comes in fun colours like Citrus, Blush, and Indigo.

There aren't many significant retail discounts on the MacBook Neo right now, but Apple offers refurbished versions that are $100 to $120 cheaper than retail. Apple Certified Refurbished products come with the same one-year warranty, look like new, and have every major component replaced. There won't be any scratches or battery wear issues.

  • MacBook Neo: 256GB storage, 8GB memory—$689 on Amazon ($10 off)
  • MacBook Neo: 512GB storage, 8GB memory, Touch ID—$799 on Amazon
  • Refurbished MacBook Neo: 256GB storage, 8GB memory—$599 on Apple Store
  • Refurbished MacBook Neo: 512GB storage, 8GB memory, Touch ID—$679 on Apple Store

MacBook Pro

The MacBook Pro is the top-of-the-line model in the lineup. You can get the best of the best, but there's an important caveat. Apple is reportedly going to redesign the high-end MacBook Pro later this year, featuring an OLED display, touch functionality, and a thinner chassis.

However, that redesign will debut only with the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips—so if you're someone buying the base model with the M5 chip, there's no problem at all with buying a new MacBook right now. Even if you don't care about the redesign at all, the M5 Pro and M5 Max are already excellent new chips.
